relations.subject: sgw:rbac-user
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted requiredForApiAccess, subject=credential, object=the gated surface, matching the pattern already established for sgw:rbac-user/sgw:admin-rest-api in secure-sgw-access.json). Resolution of the round's second watch-for question: this page's own sentence names only 'Sync Gateway RBAC controls' without saying which of the three role-shaped systems (sgw:rbac-user vs sgw:role) it means. manage-audit-logs.md (same batch) resolves it: that page defines the 'cbs' domain as 'Users that are RBAC controlled...created on Couchbase Server...Sync Gateway's Admin and Metrics REST APIs are authenticated using Couchbase Server users', and defines the separate 'sgw' domain (which is where sgw:role's channel-grant bundles live) as unrelated Sync-Gateway-only users/roles. Audit log viewing/management happens exclusively through the bootstrap config file and the Admin REST API (per manage-audit-logs.md's own enumeration), so 'RBAC controls' here means sgw:rbac-user, not sgw:role.
relations.evidence: Logs are immutable and cannot be altered once recorded. Viewing and managing audit logs permissions are enforced through Sync Gateway RBAC controls. Logs are written locally on each Sync Gateway node.

notable_absence.finding: 'Event auditing occurs per Sync Gateway node, capturing its own events only. If you require a cluster-wide record, the records must be manually consolidated by an adminstrator.' This is close to verbatim to security:auditing's own promoted note ('individual per node records must be manually consolidated by the administrator') - a striking wording parallel across two different products' documentation, but no cross-product relation is recorded here because neither page states the two mechanisms are related; recorded as a finding rather than a relation per the no-silent-merge rule. Also: no field or event on this page (or audit-log-events.md) states any severity/alerting behaviour (Info/Warning/Critical, or triggersAlert) the way Capella's monitoring:event does - reinforcing that a merge with monitoring:event would misrepresent this feature's capabilities in either direction.

cross_component_finding: This page's own text explicitly leaves the RBAC-controls sentence underspecified ('Viewing and managing audit logs permissions are enforced through Sync Gateway RBAC controls') without saying which of Sync Gateway's identity systems it means; access-control-concepts.md (a different component, linked from manage-audit-logs.md's cbs/sgw domain definitions) is what actually disambiguates it to sgw:rbac-user rather than sgw:role. See the requiredForApiAccess relation above for the full resolution and the deciding quote.
cross_product_finding: Sync Gateway's audit-logging.md describes a fourth/fifth genuinely independent audit mechanism in this ontology, alongside Server's security:auditing and Capella's monitoring:activity-log/monitoring:event. All four share surface vocabulary (timestamped, per-actor, action-based event records) but nothing in this page equates them: no sentence here says 'like Server's auditing' or 'the same as Capella's Activity Log'. Structural differences that would make a silent merge wrong: this feature is opt-in and disabled by default (per manage-audit-logs.md, 'Audit Logging on Sync Gateway is opt-in functionality and is disabled by default'), events carry no severity enum (unlike monitoring:event's Info/Warning/Critical) and no alerting behaviour (unlike triggersAlert), and logs are per-node with only manual cross-node consolidation (matching security:auditing's own per-node shape, but never stated as the SAME per-node mechanism). Kept as its own sgw:audit-logging/sgw:audit-event concept pair per the standing no-silent-merge rule.
